question_text: Determine the maximum allowable temperature that will produce a flux of less than 2000 H atoms $/\left(\mathrm{cm}^2 \cdot \mathrm{~s}\right)$ through a BCC iron foil when the concentration gradient is $-5 \times 10^{16} \frac{\text { atoms }}{\mathrm{cm}^3 \mathrm{~cm}}$. (Note the negative sign for the flux.)The unit of the answer is °C.
response:
## Solution

**Fick's first law** (steady-state diffusion through the foil):

$$J = -D\frac{dC}{dx}$$

With the given gradient $dC/dx = -5\times10^{16}\ \text{atoms/cm}^4$ (negative), the flux points in $+x$:

$$J = -D(-5\times10^{16}) = 5\times10^{16}\,D$$

(The note about the negative sign refers to the gradient convention — the flux comes out opposite in sign to the gradient.)

Set the flux equal to the limiting value to find the **maximum** $D$ (and hence maximum $T$):

$$5\times10^{16}\,D = 2000 \;\Rightarrow\; D = 4\times10^{-14}\ \text{cm}^2/\text{s} = 4\times10^{-18}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}$$

**Arrhenius diffusion coefficient** for **H in BCC iron** — taking the paired $(D_0, Q_d)$ from the same diffusion table, same phase (BCC α-Fe), same species (H in Fe), per the pairing constraint:

- $D_0 = 1.2\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}$
- $Q_d = 15\,000\ \text{J/mol}$
- $R = 8.314\ \text{J/(mol·K)}$

$$D = D_0\,e^{-Q_d/RT} \;\Rightarrow\; T = \frac{Q_d}{R\ln(D_0/D)}$$

$$\ln\!\left(\frac{D_0}{D}\right) = \ln\!\left(\frac{1.2\times10^{-4}}{4\times10^{-18}}\right) = \ln(3.0\times10^{13}) = 31.03$$

$$T = \frac{15\,000}{8.314 \times 31.03} = 58.1\ \text{K}$$

$$T = 58.1 - 273.15 = -215\ ^\circ\text{C}$$

**Model-validity check:** Hydrogen diffuses extremely fast in BCC iron (very low $Q_d$), so at room temperature the flux would be $\sim10^{14}$ atoms/(cm²·s) — vastly above 2000. Driving the flux down to 2000 therefore requires a cryogenic temperature. The result $T\approx58$ K is positive, finite, and lies **within the BCC α-Fe stability field** (stable from 0 K up to 912 °C) — no phase boundary (α→γ at 912 °C, Curie at 770 °C) is crossed. It is, however, far below the typical Arrhenius fitting range, so the value is an extrapolation (the problem explicitly invokes the single-segment Arrhenius model).

The maximum allowable temperature is therefore:

$$\boxed{-215}$$
